coverage_gaps: The merged universe is still strongest in semiconductor physical supply-chain nodes; cybersecurity, automation and niche software/data plumbing remain under-sourced and should be validated with primary filings and product-level evidence in Layer 2.
Several international candidates require current market-cap verification and ticker/exchange normalization before dashboard ranking, especially Taiwan, Japan and Europe listings.
Advanced packaging substrate candidates need primary-source confirmation of AI/HPC revenue share, customer concentration, capacity expansion timing, ABF supply access and margin sensitivity.
High-purity quartz remains a critical shadow node, but much of the direct exposure appears private or embedded inside larger materials/wafer companies; public-market mapping is still incomplete.

Data-center power/cooling candidates are included mostly as hypotheses or inferences; need backlog, customer and product-level evidence to distinguish true AI bottleneck exposure from broad electrification/industrial demand.
Market-pricing checks are not performed in Layer 1C; no valuation, target price, buy/sell or return conclusion is included.
Analyst coverage and media-attention scores are provisional; a later layer should quantify coverage count, ownership concentration, short interest, factor crowding and recent price reaction.

memory_update.text: Technology theme should be treated as an AI/cloud infrastructure buildout that pulls on physical semiconductor capacity, advanced packaging, optical connectivity, power/cooling infrastructure, cybersecurity and automation rather than as a single mega-cap software or GPU theme.

Semiconductor equipment subsystem suppliers remain the highest-conviction underfollowed lane because they sit below visible equipment OEMs and can benefit from qualification lock-in across vacuum, power delivery, gas/chemical delivery, process control and contamination-control subsystems.
Advanced packaging substrate materials and capacity, especially ABF/build-up film and high-end substrate suppliers, should be tracked as a core AI accelerator bottleneck lane.
AI optical connectivity should be mapped below transceiver assemblers into lasers, silicon photonics, compound-semiconductor wafers, epitaxy capacity and epitaxy tools.
High-purity quartz remains a systemic but difficult-to-express public-market shadow bottleneck; public candidates should be treated cautiously unless direct revenue or dependency evidence is found.

Cybersecurity, automation and data-center power/cooling candidates need primary-source validation before they can be ranked with the same confidence as semiconductor subsystem and packaging-material candidates.
Layer 2 should verify market-cap buckets, analyst coverage, revenue purity, customer concentration, qualification cycles, capacity constraints, and recent pricing/crowding for all candidates.

summary: Merged Layer 1 universe for Technology using Serenity's chokepoint lens. The highest-priority initial universe is not centered on mega-cap AI platforms, but on the physical and digital supply-chain layers that AI/cloud growth pulls on: semiconductor equipment subsystems, high-purity process materials, advanced packaging substrates and build-up films, optical connectivity and compound-semiconductor tools, data-center power/cooling infrastructure, and selected cloud-security/automation control layers. Current evidence is strongest for semiconductor subsystem suppliers, ABF/substrate bottlenecks, high-purity quartz dependency, and optical/epitaxy toolchains. Cybersecurity, automation, and data-center infrastructure remain important but need additional primary-source Layer 2 validation.
